title: Attention: how AI knows what 'it' means
label: EP 27

yt.title: What is 'it'?
notes: '...because it was too tired' -> the animal
'...because it was too wide' -> the street
One word changes the meaning

lines.text: 'The animal didn't cross the street because it was too tired.' [1] 'It' is the animal. [2] Change one word: 'too wide'... [3] and 'it' becomes the street. How does an AI know?

yt.title: One word at a time
notes: Older models read word by word
A summary is passed along, like a whisper
Long sentences: the start gets blurry

lines.text: Older models, before Transformers, read one word at a time, [1] passing a summary along, like a whisper down a long line. [2] By the end, the start of the sentence has gone blurry.

yt.title: Look back, pick what matters
notes: Each word looks back at earlier words
'tired' links 'it' to 'animal'
'wide' links 'it' to 'street'

lines.text: Attention fixes that. [1] Each word can look back at every word before it, and decide which ones matter. [2] When the model reaches 'tired', it looks back... [3] and links 'it' to 'animal'. [4] Make it 'wide', and the link jumps to 'street'.

yt.title: Question, name tag, meaning
notes: Query: the question a word asks
Key: the name tag each word wears
Value: the meaning it borrows

lines.text: How does it pick? [1] 'It' asks a question: 'who am I talking about?' [2] Every earlier word wears a name tag. 'I'm a living thing.' 'I'm a place.' [3] The best match gets the most attention. [4] Then 'it' borrows that word's meaning. Engineers call these: query, key, value.

yt.title: Why long chats get slow
notes: Every word checks every other word
2x the prompt = about 4x the attention work
That's why context has limits

lines.text: Here's the catch. [1] Every word checks every other word. [2] Double your prompt, and the attention work roughly quadruples. [3] That's why very long chats get slow, and why they have limits.

yt.title: The T in ChatGPT
notes: Google, 2017: 'Attention Is All You Need'
A model built entirely from attention: the Transformer
GPT = Generative Pre-trained Transformer

lines.text: In 2017, Google built a model entirely out of attention: [1] the Transformer. [2] That's the T in ChatGPT.

yt.title: The trophy and the suitcase
notes: '...because it was too big' -> ?
'...because it was too small' -> ?
Big: the trophy. Small: the suitcase.

lines.text: Your turn. 'The trophy didn't fit in the suitcase because it was too big.' What is 'it'? [1] And if it was too small? <pause 2> [2] Too big: the trophy. Too small: the suitcase.
